label: Morning Brief
timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, stocks fell Tuesday on hotter-than-expected inflation data and AI worries, and yields jumped (Nov 10, 4:54 PM and 4:17 PM ET). After the close, WSJ reported CoreWeave met Wall Street expectations with its backlog at $133 billion and shares rising (5:14 PM ET). Overnight, WSJ reported Nasdaq futures led stock futures higher as AI optimism returned (4:16 AM ET) and European chip stocks climbed after CoreWeave's results (4:25 AM ET); Bloomberg tied the rebound to demand for Anthropic's IPO (5:46 AM ET). WSJ reported Asian bond yields rose on expectations for a Fed rate hike (1:37 AM ET), the dollar reached a four-week high (4:55 AM ET), and Brent crude rose above $92 a barrel after a sharp selloff (3:02 AM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

calendar.text: US Treasury market closed for Veterans Day, per WSJ (headline and summary only)

cryptoDriver.text: CoinDesk reported bitcoin sat out the stock rebound as ETF outflows extended to a fourth day.

items.headline: Law Firm Wachtell Lipton to Lead Nvidia Internal Investigation
items.summary: Per WSJ, the New York law firm will lead Nvidia's internal investigation into whether the company was the target of a foreign espionage effort. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's Bull Case Hinges on Huang Surviving China Spy Probe
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's investigation of CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy is raising questions about the company's future and sending its stock into a tailspin. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Scandal Tests the Resilience of the Global AI Boom
items.summary: Per WSJ, the article asks whether the AI boom could carry on without Jensen Huang, described as its biggest cheerleader. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Citigroup lowers Nvidia price target to $285 from $315, keeps Buy
items.summary: Citigroup kept its Buy rating on Nvidia and lowered its price target from $315 to $285, per Yahoo Finance analyst data.

items.headline: Wells Fargo lowers Nvidia price target to $300 from $315, keeps Overweight
items.summary: Wells Fargo kept its Overweight rating on Nvidia and lowered its price target from $315 to $300, per Yahoo Finance analyst data.
